association_evidence.supports: Artek identifies Stool 60 as Alvar Aalto's 1933 design, specifies three legs and a solid-birch edge band, describes its Finnish/modernist design context and continuous production, and labels the selected variant birch with clear lacquer. This identifies the product version, not a particular object's manufacture date.

The Alvar Aalto Foundation identifies the three-legged Stool 60, design Alvar Aalto 1933, and explains the L-leg bending and stacking system. Its page separately labels E60 as the four-legged variation; this prevents mixing the two models. It does not authenticate the individual product visual as a historic physical specimen.

confusion_check.discriminating_relationships: Use documented Finnish design context together with the round seat, three-leg arrangement and bent front leg/seat relationships. Allow broader modernist overlap. The three visible legs and Artek product identity distinguish Stool 60 from four-legged E60; pale wood alone does not identify Nordic design.
